Members of a Markov equivalence class

Source: R/class_members.R
mc_class_members.Rd

Enumerates the directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) that a completed partially directed acyclic graph (CPDAG) stands for: the acyclic orientations of its undirected edges that keep every directed edge and introduce no v-structure (immorality) the class does not have. By the characterization of Markov equivalence by skeleton and v-structures (Verma and Pearl, 1990; Andersson, Madigan and Perlman, 1997), these are exactly the DAGs of the equivalence class. The members imply the same separations, so observational data that carry only those constraints do not distinguish among them. For a partially directed graph that is not a CPDAG, such as one oriented further by background knowledge, the same enumeration returns its consistent DAG extensions.

Usage

mc_class_members(cpdag, max_members = 1000L)

Arguments

cpdag

a square 0/1 adjacency matrix in the package convention (an undirected edge has both entries one, an arc \(i \to j\) only [i, j]), or an object of class "mcg_cpdag".

max_members

a single positive integer; the enumeration stops after this many members and reports the truncation.

Value

A list of adjacency matrices, one per member, each a DAG in the same convention and with the dimnames of cpdag. The list carries the attribute "truncated", TRUE when max_members was reached before the enumeration ended. The list is empty when the graph admits no consistent extension.

How they are enumerated

One undirected edge is oriented at a time, both ways, Meek's rules propagate the consequences, and a branch is abandoned as soon as it creates a cycle or an immorality the class does not have. Because the two branches fix opposite directions on the same edge, no member is produced twice. The count grows quickly with the number of undirected edges, so max_members caps it and the result says whether the cap was reached.

References

Verma, T. and Pearl, J. (1990). Equivalence and synthesis of causal models. Proceedings of the 6th Conference on Uncertainty in Artificial Intelligence, 220-227.

Andersson, S. A., Madigan, D. and Perlman, M. D. (1997). A characterization of Markov equivalence classes for acyclic digraphs. The Annals of Statistics 25(2), 505-541. doi:10.1214/aos/1031833662

Meek, C. (1995). Causal inference and causal explanation with background knowledge. Proceedings of the 11th Conference on Uncertainty in Artificial Intelligence, 403-410.

See also

mc_class_coefficients for what the members disagree about, mc_orient_meek for the propagation rules.

Other equivalence class: mc_class_coefficients(), mc_sid()

Examples

# the chain 1 - 2 - 3 has three members, the collider none of them
a <- matrix(0L, 3, 3)
a[1, 2] <- a[2, 1] <- a[2, 3] <- a[3, 2] <- 1L
length(mc_class_members(a))
#> [1] 3
